record.what_it_does: Stripe provides an API for accepting payments, managing subscriptions, billing, payouts, and other financial/fintech operations for online businesses.
record.auth_notes: Standard API access is via secret/restricted API keys sent as the HTTP Basic Auth username (or as a Bearer token for cross-origin requests). OAuth2 exists but is scoped to Stripe Connect (platforms authorizing access to a connected merchant's account), not general first-party API access. The official MCP server supports both OAuth (recommended) and restricted API key as a bearer token.
record.access_notes: Anyone can sign up for a Stripe account and immediately get test-mode secret keys (prefix sk_test_) to call the full API at no cost; live-mode keys just require completing account activation (no paid plan or approval gate for API access itself).

evidence.quote: The Stripe API authenticates requests using HTTP Basic Auth. Provide your API key as the basic auth username value.
if you need to authenticate using bearer auth (for example, for a cross-origin request), use -H "Authorization: Bearer
Stripe's MCP server uses OAuth to authorize clients according to the MCP specification.
Test secret keys have the prefix sk_test_ and live mode secret keys have the prefix sk_live_.
The Stripe Model Context Protocol (MCP) server provides tools that AI agents can use to interact with the Stripe API
Stripe can push real-time event data to your application's webhook endpoint when events happen in your Stripe account.
This repository contains OpenAPI specifications for Stripe's API.
